This is a nonpersonal services contract requesting software development of Autonomy Government Reference Architecture (A-GRA) interfaces for the Mission Termination System (MTS), yielding a Technology Readiness Level 9 (TRL 9) product . MTS is a Run Time Assurance (RTA) tool based on the Testing Autonomy in Complex Environments (TACE) code base created by Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Lab (JHU APL). MTS is used at Edwards AFB to safely test autonomous control of small Unmanned Aerial Systems (sUAS). The government shall not exercise any supervision or control over the contract service providers performing the services herein. Such contract service providers shall be accountable solely to the contractor who, in turn, is responsible to the government. 1.1.1 Description of Services/Objectives. ion. 1.6.3 Delivered product shall integrate A-GRA autonomy interface into the existing MTS Service Set creation tool. The platform enables concept-level editing, bulk editing, and semantic alignment of textual subject indexing and research data attributes. The primary function of the system is semantic curation and workflow support. Requirements Technical Support (Ongoing) The contractor shall provide continued operational support for the VocBench open-source platform, including: Supporting NAL staff or contractors with the migration from the current Sandbox environment to NAL-managed cloud servers, including configuration, testing, data validation, and transition activities. This is the final effort of the VocBench portion NALT machine age program out of the sandbox and operational. This work should be completed within one year of award. Support for Maintenance of existing configurations for NALT and related vocabularies, and ultimately for NAL staff or contractors to perform this

approximately 5-10 tickets be user per year. This will be on-going effort during the migration from the sandbox, and for four (1) one-year options after the migration. Responding to support requests within two (2) business days. Training (As Needed / Refresher) The contractor shall provide refresher or targeted training sessions as needed, including: Training on new VocBench features, workflows, or administrative options. As-needed onboarding for new staff or community editors. All training may be delivered virtually. Training sessions are typically about 4 hours in nature and can be all at once or over a few days as needed for the material. STATEMENT OF WORK C. 1. OVERVIEW/BACKGROUND. The Library of Congress (Library) requires a contractor to produce, maintain, and support the latest generation of Digital Talking Book Machine (DTBM) devices, known as the DA2 (DTBM model Digital Advanced version 2), which were originally launched June 18, 2025. The National Library Service for the Blind and Print Disabled (NLS) provides free books and magazines in audio and braille format to eligible U.S. residents and citizens living abroad. NLS’ enabling legislation was changed in 2016 (Public Law 114-219) to permit NLS to develop and distribute devices to be used for reading any format, including DAISY (Digital Accessible Information System). As part of these services and products offered, NLS loans free DTBMs for use in consuming NLS-produced audio materials. NLS-produced audio materials are distributed via NLS DTBM cartridges and data files online via Braille and Audio Reading Download (BARD) website in AMR-WB+, MPEG I/Layer 3 (MP3), RIFF WAV, and other audio formats. NLS requires additional DA2 units, consistent with the existing inventory

The Library of Congress (Library) requires a contractor to produce, maintain, and support the latest generation of Digital Talking Book Machine (DTBM) devices, known as the DA2 (DTBM model Digital Advanced version 2), which were originally launched June 18, 2025. The National Library Service for the Blind and Print Disabled (NLS) provides free books and magazines in audio and braille format to eligible U.S. residents and citizens living abroad. NLS’ enabling legislation was changed in 2016 (Public Law 114-219) to permit NLS to develop and distribute devices to be used for reading any format, including DAISY (Digital Accessible Information System). As part of these services and products offered, NLS loans free DTBMs for use in consuming NLS-produced audio materials. NLS-produced audio materials are distributed via NLS DTBM cartridges and data files online via Braille and Audio Reading Download (BARD) website in AMR-WB+, MPEG I/Layer 3 (MP3), RIFF WAV, and other audio formats. NLS requires additional DA2 units, consistent with the existing inventory of NLS DA2 devices. NLS requires quantities suffi

The Government is in no way obligated to make an award, nor to pay any costs incurred by the Contractor in preparing and submitting its quote. 1.1 PURPOSE AND BACKGROUND This Statement of Work (SOW) establishes the requirements for the acquisition and deployment of Think Trends Software, an Agentic AI technology platform, to support FDA adverse event reporting workflows. Think Trends Software will be leveraged for its AI -powered Document Processing and Agentic Optical Character Recognition (OCR) capabilities to streamline adverse eve

erse experiences, product use patterns, health effects, consumer narratives, and product category information. D. Case Validation, Quality Control, and Human-in-the-Loop Review Think Trends Software shall incorporate validation agents to compare extracted data against business rules, required fields, confidence thresholds, terminology standards, and case -processing logic. Records that meet defined thresholds may proceed automatically, while exceptions shall be routed for human review. Key quality-control features include: • Confidence scoring at field, document, and case levels. • Source traceability to page, section, table, and line references. • Automated flagging of missing, inconsistent, conflicting, or low-confidence data. • Human-in-the-loop review screens for case processors and safety reviewers. • Reviewer acceptance, correction, override, and approval workflows. • Full audit trail of AI extraction, human edits, and final approved values. E. Data Standardization and Regulatory Output Generation Think Trends Software shall transform extracted adverse event information into structured formats required for case management, analytics, and downstream regulatory processing. The platform shall support configurable mappings to FDA data standards, Center-specific systems, XM

CVM, CDRH, CTP, and HFP to configure unique workflows, data models, rules, and outputs. 3. End -to-End Adverse Event Case Automation: Think Trends Software supports intake, classification, extraction, validation, triage, routing, human review, data transformation, and downstream submission/output generation. 4. Human-in-the-Loop Regulatory Control: The system keeps FDA reviewers in control by allowing them to review, correct, approve, or override AI-generated outputs before final case acceptance. 5. Explainability and Source Traceability: Each extracted field can be traced back to the original source document, page, section, and text reference, supporting transparency, auditability, and reviewer confidence. 6. Confidence-Based Processing: Think Trends Software assigns confidence scores to extracted data and automatically routes low-confidence or inconsistent records for human review. 7. Multi -Document and Multi -Format Processing: Think Trends Software shall process scanned PDFs, structured forms, unstructured narratives, tables, handwritten content where feasible, images, attachments, correspondence, and supporting records. 8. Duplicate and Follow -Up Detection: AI agents shall compare incoming submissions against existing records to identify potential duplicates, follow-

The Mechanistic Toxicology Branch (MTB) within the DTT conducts laboratory research to identify human health hazards and understand environmental toxicity through hybrid basic and applied science approaches that include development of new approach methods (NAMs) for toxicology research. The MTB is pioneering innovative toxicology research with advanced cell systems such as human tissue chips and 3D organoid models to understand the adverse effects of chemicals, drugs, and natural pr

public health through development of data and knowledge that are translatable, predictive, and timely. The Mechanistic Toxicology Branch (MTB) within the DTT conducts laboratory research to identify human health hazards and understand environmental toxicity through hybrid basic and applied science approaches that include development of new approach methods (NAMs) for toxicology research. The MTB is pioneering innovative toxicology research with advanced cell systems such as human tissue chips and 3D organoid models to understand the adverse effects of chemicals, drugs, and natural products and develop innovative solutions for translational toxicology research. 2) Objectives: The MTB seeks to solve ongoing challenges in the scalable generation of 3D human organoid/spheroid models by exploring the potential of microencapsulation technology to bioengineer human tissue models that better reflect human physiology for translational toxicology research. A Fluigent Microencapsulation System has been identified as uniquely suited for our exploratory research needs to model toxicity-induced liver fibrosis with 3D microtissue models. This work is funded by an external NIH grant in collaboration with NCATS through a Complement-ARIE grant award to develop human- based m

e approaches that include development of new approach methods (NAMs) for toxicology research. The MTB is pioneering innovative toxicology research with advanced cell systems such as human tissue chips and 3D organoid models to understand the adverse effects of chemicals, drugs, and natural products and develop innovative solutions for translational toxicology research. 2) Objectives: The MTB seeks to solve ongoing challenges in the scalable generation of 3D human organoid/spheroid models by exploring the potential of microencapsulation technology to bioengineer human tissue models that better reflect human physiology for translational toxicology research. A Fluigent Microencapsulation System has been identified as uniquely suited for our exploratory research needs to model toxicity-induced liver fibrosis with 3D microtissue models. This work is funded by an external NIH grant in collaboration with NCATS through a Complement-ARIE grant award to develop human- based microphysiological systems and test methods that better model human health (in this case, the initial work will focus on liver). 3) Scope: The Contractor shall provide a Fluigent Microencapsulation Platform, in accordance with the obtained vendor quotation. The system shall include the require

formation of three-dimensional (3D) microtissues and organoids. The Contractor shall also provide installation and training for the Fluigent system at the NIEHS facility. Vendor representatives shall perform system setup and provide training to facilitate rapid onboarding and use of the technology. The system will operate independently of NIEHS information technology (IT) systems and will not require NIEHS IT support. The computer and software components are expected to be delivered by the end of September 2026. Full system installation and training are expected to be completed in Fall 2026, subject to vendor engineer scheduling availability. Work shall be performed at NIEHS, Rall Building 101, Laboratories E144–146.
